dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. How can I help you?
Hi, Denise. Yes, my name is Min-jun Rahman. I'm calling about a storm drain, well, a grate, at the curb. I'm sorry, I'm on my cell and I only have a few minutes.
That's fine, go ahead. What's going on with it?

So the grate has sunk. It's dropped down below the level of the pavement, maybe three inches, I'd say, actually closer to four. And when it rains, the water goes everywhere but down it. It runs right past and pools across the whole low spot in the street.
Okay. Was that during the storm this past weekend?

Yes. The nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday. It was bad Saturday night, and it was still standing water yesterday afternoon, Sunday, around four o'clock. And this isn't the first time. It does it every time we get a real rain, and I've been watching it do that for a while now.
I'm sorry, that's a nuisance. Can I get the address or the nearest cross street?
I'd rather not go into the address on this call, if that's all right. I can describe it, it's the grate on the corner by the old stone wall. Can you not just send somebody to look at it?
I do usually need a location to put in a work order. But let me ask you this, is anybody's property getting water, or is it just the street?

It's the street and the sidewalk, mostly. The thing is, I have a neighbor, an older woman, she's in her eighties, and she can't get out when it's like that. She won't step through that water. Sunday she couldn't get to her car, and she had an appointment she missed, I believe it was Monday, no, she said it was this morning. Either way, she's stuck.
Oh, that's not good. Okay, that does make it a priority to get looked at.
That's what I'm saying. I own the building, I'm the landlord, so I hear about it from my tenants too. Nobody's come out. I'm not blaming you personally, but it keeps happening and nothing gets done.

No, I hear you. After a storm like that the crews are stretched thin, but a sunken grate is something they'd want to see. So who do you call? You call us, and I can log it. If you give me the street, I'll put it in as a drainage and catch basin repair request, and they'll send someone out to check it.
Right. Well, my question was really who I should call to have it checked, and I suppose the answer is you.
It's us, yes. Public Works handles the catch basins. I can also take a callback number so the supervisor can reach you if they have questions.

Okay. It's four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-eight-zero. That's my cell. I'll be honest, I work in a school cafeteria, I'm a lunch worker, and this is the only quiet minute I get all day. Lunch service starts again in about two minutes.
Then let's get this done. Give me just the street name, even without a number, and I'll write it up while you're on.
I understand. I'm going to have to call back with that, because I need to look at something and I'm out of time. Could you note that I called, Monday, one-forty or so, about a sunken grate?
I'll make a note with your name and number. When you call back, ask for me, Denise, and we'll finish it.
Thank you. I'll call tomorrow. Goodbye.
Okay, take care. Bye-bye.
